extracted.intended_audience: learned Christians, theologians, clergy, and civil rulers (readers of theological/political treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for determining when a purported prophet or miracle is genuine, how to distinguish natural from supernatural causes, and who has authority to adjudicate such claims in a Christian commonwealth. Focuses on Biblical tests, purpose of miracles, and the role of the sovereign/church in public belief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of a pretended prophet's calling
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man ought to examine the probability of a pretended prophet's calling; men had need to be very circumspect, and wary, in obeying the voice of man that pretends himself to be a Prophet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because such a one pretends to govern men and rule over them, his claim is likely to be suspect of ambition and imposture. Examine by reason and judgment to discern between natural and supernatural gifts, and do not obey until examined, unless the prophet is authorized by the civil sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural marks for true prophets (Old Testament)
rubrics_metrics.description: One Old Testament rule: conformable doctrine to that which Moses the sovereign prophet had taught; and the other the miraculous power of foretelling what God would bring to pass (Deut. 13, Deut. 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a prophet teaches a different religion than that established by God's lieutenant (e.g., Moses), do not take him for a prophet. Also test predictions: if the praediction does not come to pass, reject the prophet (citing Deut. 18:22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scriptural mark for true prophets (New Testament)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the New Testament the principal mark is the preaching of this Doctrine, that Jesus is the Christ (confessing that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh) (1 John 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every Spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God; every Spirit that confesseth not that he is come in the flesh is not of Christ (the Spirit of Antichrist). Thus denial of that article marks a false prophet regardless of miracles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and authorization: exception for sovereign prophet
rubrics_metrics.description: All prophecy but of the sovereign prophet is to be examined by every subject; unless the prophet is the civil sovereign or authorized by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prophet is the civil sovereign or authorized by the sovereign, subjects may defer; otherwise use private and public reason to test claims. In a commonwealth, the sovereign or lawful head of the church is the judge in doubtful cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a miracle
rubrics_metrics.description: "A MIRACLE, is a work of God, (besides his operation by the way of Nature, ordained in the Creation,) done for the making manifest to his elect, the mission of an extraordinary Minister for their salvation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miracles are not merely admirable works but works beyond ordinary natural operations, performed to manifest the mission of an extraordinary minister and to procure credit to God's messengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rarity and lack of natural cause as conditions of miraclehood
rubrics_metrics.description: A miracle must be strange (rare) and such that we cannot imagine it to have been done by natural means; if a natural cause is known or imaginable, it ceases to be a miracle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the first rainbow was a miracle; once frequent and explicable (rainbows), they are no longer miracles. If human art or natural science explains the event, do not call it miraculous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose criterion: miracles must serve to authenticate God's messengers
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of miracles is to procure credit to God's messengers, ministers, and prophets, so men may know they are called and sent by God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Great works not done to procure credit to a prophet (e.g., creation, universal flood) are not commonly called miracles in this ecclesiastical sense. Miracles are signs intended to confirm a minister's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-relative judgement: what seems a miracle to one may not to another
rubrics_metrics.description: Admiration and wonder depend on knowledge and experience; the same event may be a miracle to the ignorant but not to those who know its natural cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate purported miracles against the observer's knowledge of natural causes; be skeptical of reports where natural explanations (astronomy, trickery, stagecraft) plausibly exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: No created spirit or magician can produce a true miracle
rubrics_metrics.description: No devil, angel, or other created spirit can do a miracle; if an effect is produced by enchantment or human art then it is not an immediate work of God and thus not a miracle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparent parallels in Scripture where magicians 'did likewise' should be interpreted as imposture or natural arts rather than true miracles. Distinguish immediate divine action from human or diabolical artifices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspect imposture and natural deception
rubrics_metrics.description: Men are apt to be deceived by false miracles: jugglery, confederacy, ventriloquism, secret intelligence, and deceit can produce the appearance of wonders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the many easy means of deception (confederate cures, staged events) before ascribing supernatural origin. Use investigation to rule out imposture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public vs private assent to miracles/reports
rubrics_metrics.description: If we see no miracle but only hear of it, consult the lawful Church (God's lieutenant). A private man may believe or not in his heart, but public confession must submit to the public (sovereign) judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public order and obedience in a commonwealth, rely on the sovereign's or lawful church head's determination about reported miracles; do not let private rumor overturn public peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard for accepting a reported miracle
rubrics_metrics.description: We must both see it done and use all means possible to consider whether it is really done and such that no natural power can do the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not see the miracle, inquire of the lawful head of the church; if he denies it, treat the claim as presumptuous (citing Deut. 18:22). If he affirms, accept as authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish ordinary spiritual 'speaking in the Spirit' from supernatural revelation
rubrics_metrics.description: To subordinate prophets of perpetual calling, God spake by the Spirit meaning natural inclinations to piety, belief, and righteousness (gifts and graces), not necessarily supernatural revelation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attribute every mention of 'the Spirit' to a supernatural, immediate divine impartation; often it denotes disposition, intention, or moral influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of legitimate non-supernatural divine operations (lots, inclinations)
rubrics_metrics.description: God sometimes spoke by lots or disposed men by natural and ordinary means; such operations are ascribed to the Spirit insofar as they incline men to piety but are not necessarily supernatural revelation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize scriptural instances (casting lots, inclinations in elders) where divine will is manifest through ordinary institutional or natural procedures; these are not necessarily miracles or direct revelations.
